metadata.description: Self-report measure of perceived stress, especially the extent to which life situations are appraised as unpredictable, uncontrollable, or overloaded.
metadata.intended_use: Research and survey assessment of perceived stress; PSS-10 and PSS-4 are separate forms and the record contains no item wording.
metadata.name_origin: Perceived Stress Scale, abbreviated PSS; the suffix identifies the item-count form such as PSS-10 or PSS-4.
metadata.development_history: Developed by Cohen, Kamarck, and Mermelstein and published in 1983 as a global measure of perceived stress.
metadata.measurement_rationale: The construct concerns appraisal of stressfulness and perceived control, not a diagnosis or a direct count of external events.
metadata.interpretation_notes: The source record notes that there are no diagnostic cutoffs; compare scores in the appropriate sample and follow the exact form's permissions and guidance.
metadata.notes: Link-only. The creator's university page directs requests through ePROVIDE; a free request is not itself permission to reuse or redistribute the form.

versions.source_citation: Cohen, S., Kamarck, T., & Mermelstein, R. (1983). A global measure of perceived stress. Journal of Health and Social Behavior, 24(4), 385-396.

source_documents.title: Perceived Stress Scale forms and permission instructions
source_documents.license_name: Permission request via ePROVIDE; public redistribution not established
source_documents.permission_basis: Carnegie Mellon directs use-permission requests for the Perceived Stress Scale through MAPI Research Trust/ePROVIDE. The request is free to submit; approval/use terms are determined by the rights holder. No item wording is included here.

metadata.notes: The source says the scale has no diagnostic cut-offs; compare within samples.

cosmin_metrics.internal_consistency: Cronbach's alpha ca. .78 (14-Item-Originalform) bzw. ca. .89 (PSS-10) in Normstichproben.
cosmin_metrics.source: Cohen S, Kamarck T, Mermelstein R (1983). A global measure of perceived stress. J Health Soc Behav, 24(4), 385-396.

versions.scoring_notes: Positiv formulierte Items werden gemäß offizieller Syntax umgepolt und anschließend summiert; es gibt keine diagnostischen Cutoffs.
versions.psychometric_summary: PSS ist häufig eingesetzt, aber Normen und Validität hängen von Form, Recall-Zeitraum und Population ab.
